1  ORDER

The petitioner is the 2nd accused in Crime No.255/2012 of Badiadukka Police Station, Kasaragod, a case relating to the commission of offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
The prosecution case is that, the petitioner along with her son, who is the husband of the defacto complainant, subjected the defacto complainant to matrimonial cruelty demanding more dowry.
The final report filed by the Badiadukka Police was taken on to files as C.C No.2221/2012 by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kasaragod.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kasaragod
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: After a full-fledged trial in the aforesaid case, with the examination of seven prosecution witnesses, and marking of six documents, the learned Magistrate acquitted the 1st accused in the crime due to paucity of evidence.
The case against the present petitioner, who was the 2 nd accused, was refiled since she had not appeared during that time before the Trial Court.

Now the petitioner is facing prosecution 2025:KER:72694 in the present case renumbered as C.C No.996/2022.
3.
In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that she is totally innocent, and that she has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further stated that, in view of the acquittal of the 1st accused in C.C No.2221/2012, the entire substratum of the prosecution case is lost, and hence there is no purpose to be fulfilled by the continuation of the proceedings against the petitioner.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
5. Annexure-A3 is the judgment rendered by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Kasaragod,
on 30.11.2019 in C.C No.2221/2012, the case against the 1 st accused in this crime.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Kasaragod
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the aforesaid judgment, the learned Magistrate has observed that the prosecution has failed to establish the offence of matrimonial cruelty as envisaged under Section 498A, IPC.
The 1st accused has been acquitted accordingly, with the finding that the evidence adduced were totally insufficient to bring forth 2025:KER:72694 the offence alleged in this case.
6. As far as the present case is concerned, it is pertinent to note that there is only superficial and omnibus allegations against the petitioner herein.

Apart from a stray statement of the defacto complainant that the petitioner had denied food to her, and also that on one occasion she had demanded dowry from the defacto complainant and her parents, there are no specific accusations against the petitioner herein.

Taking into account the above aspect, as well as the acquittal of the 1st accused, it has to be stated that no purpose would be fulfilled by the continuation of the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner herein.
7. A reading of Annexure-A3 judgment would reveal that the entire substratum of the prosecution case is lost.
In the above circumstances, the prayer of the petitioner to quash the proceedings against her, deserves to be allowed.
